analysis.title: Prime Services Weekly Report
key_insights: GS Equity Fundamental L/S performance estimate fell -1.28% between 10/16 and 10/22 vs MSCI World TR -0.76%, driven by beta of -0.98% and alpha of -0.30% on short side losses.
GS Equity Systematic L/S performance estimate fell -1.26% over the same period, driven by alpha of -1.63% on short side losses, partly offset by beta of +0.38%.

Overall book gross leverage rose 0.6 pts to 312.3% (79th percentile 1-year) and net leverage fell 0.9 pts to 71.8% (3rd percentile 1-year). Overall book L/S ratio fell 0.7% to 1.597 (3rd percentile 1-year).

Fundamental L/S gross leverage rose 0.8 pts to 211.7% (63rd percentile 1-year) while net leverage fell 1.7 pts to 47.0%, a 1-year low. Beta-adjusted fundamental net leverage fell 3.5 pts to 60.4%, also a 1-year low.
Global equities were net sold for a 3rd straight week (-0.6 SDs 1-year) as de-grossing accelerated, with long sales outpacing short covers 3.4 to 1.
Regional flows were split. North America and EM Asia were net sold, while DM Asia and Europe were net bought.
Single stocks were net sold for a 6th straight week, driven by long sales. Macro products were net bought for the first time in 3 weeks, driven by long buys.
7 of 11 global sectors were net sold, led in dollar terms by TMT sectors (Info Tech and Comm Svcs) and Energy. Staples, Real Estate and Cons Disc were the most net bought.

HFs net sold global Energy at the fastest pace in over 5 months, driven by short and long sales (1.4 to 1). Selling in Oil, Gas & Consumable Fuels outpaced modest buying in Energy Equipment & Services.

The Prime book is over-weight Energy vs MSCI World by +0.5% (89th percentile 1-year, 69th percentile 5-year). Gross/net Energy allocations are 4.9%/4.8% of the book, in the 90th/95th percentiles 1-year.

Staples was the most net bought global sector in dollar terms, at the fastest pace in 10 weeks, driven by long buys and short covers (1.4 to 1). Buying was led by Staples Distribution & Retail, Personal Care Products and Household Products.
The Prime book is under-weight Staples vs MSCI World by -3.7% (38th percentile 1-year). Gross/net Staples allocations are 4.6%/1.4%.
Europe saw the largest regional flow changes, with long sales of -1.72 SDs and short covers of +1.37 SDs. Health Care had long sales of -1.57 SDs and Comm Svcs had short sales of -2.01 SDs.
